breadth_freeze.rule: New top-level domains require an ADR proving existing volumes cannot represent the requirement.

laws: models propose; deterministic control planes authorize and commit
provider-native objects terminate at adapter boundaries
child authority is a subset of parent authority
writes require idempotency or explicit compensation semantics
self-improvement produces candidates; promotion is gated
SOTA status requires reproducible comparative evidence

volumes.title: Plan Constitution
requirements: Define authoritative precedence among runtime truth, construction authority, target plan and evidence.
Freeze top-level breadth at VOL-420 unless an ADR proves existing domains are insufficient.
Require signed, timestamped, evidence-backed accountability for completion-bearing work.
risks: parallel planning systems bypassing canonical authority
gaps: continue deepening remaining volumes beyond current depth passes
bind future ADR workflow to explicit review/promotion rules

volumes.title: Scientific & Historical Foundation
requirements: Preserve scientific claims with source, method, result, limitation and correction/retraction lineage.
Track historical techniques by problem/mechanism/failure mode/modern analogue instead of citation popularity.
Separate replication status and negative results from narrative confidence.
risks: retracted/corrected findings surviving as current truth
gaps: cross-source citation graph needs executable reconciliation

volumes.title: System Architecture
requirements: Maintain one canonical architecture graph for roots, ownership zones, runtime DAGs and interfaces.
Reject illegal dependencies and undeclared production components before dependency-heavy tests.
Represent target/current drift as explicit gaps rather than implicit exceptions.
gaps: expand architecture fitness checks to all generated/runtime components
automate owner lookup for newly created paths

volumes.title: Canonical Contract System
requirements: Give every serialized contract stable identity, owner, version, compatibility rule and migration semantics.
Fail closed on ambiguous security-sensitive serialization including duplicate keys/non-finite values.
Define absent/null, unknown-enum, canonicalization and cross-runtime numeric/text semantics.
gaps: complete producer/consumer inventory for every canonical contract

volumes.title: Kernel & Execution Foundation
requirements: Bootstrap services in deterministic dependency order with explicit readiness and shutdown semantics.
Propagate cancellation, deadline, budget and operation identity through all runtime layers.
Prevent orphan work and unbounded background execution after terminal operation state.
gaps: unify service supervision semantics across backend and engine
expand cancellation propagation coverage into all connectors

volumes.title: Data & Persistence
requirements: Declare authoritative, derived, cache and ephemeral state classes with one canonical owner each.
Use transactional/outbox or explicit compensation semantics for cross-boundary durable changes.
Define migration, backup, restore, deletion and retention behavior for every persistent class.
gaps: add migration compatibility rehearsal to release qualification

volumes.title: Model Development Program
requirements: Version training data with rights, integrity, deduplication, contamination and PII metadata.
Bind every model artifact to exact data/code/config/hardware/evaluation lineage.
Keep research/training candidates isolated from production promotion authority.
gaps: native training infrastructure remains a target capability

volumes.title: Inference Engine
requirements: Expose provider-neutral inference with streaming, cancellation, structured output and bounded retries.
Treat caches/batching/speculation as optimizations that cannot alter semantic correctness.
Record usage, latency, provider/model identity and terminal reason for every request.
gaps: continuous batching and local serving need dedicated implementation
speculative decoding requires measured correctness gates

volumes.title: Model Routing
requirements: Route by capability, policy, privacy/data boundary, reliability, latency and cost constraints.
Make fallback an explicit decision that cannot silently weaken residency/privacy/security requirements.
Persist route rationale and usage for evaluation and replay.
gaps: add learned-routing experiments only behind champion/challenger evaluation

volumes.title: Context Engineering
requirements: Compile immutable policy, user objective, durable state, authorized memory/retrieval, tools and model constraints into typed context.
Preserve trust classification and provenance through truncation, compression and reordering.
Budget tokens by authority and task value without allowing untrusted content to displace mandatory policy.
gaps: add semantic compression with invariant checks
measure context utility versus cost across task classes

volumes.title: Memory System
requirements: Separate working, conversation, episodic, semantic, procedural, project and artifact memory classes.
Gate durable memory writes through privacy, deduplication, contradiction and promotion rules.
Support deletion/retention propagation into derived embeddings/indexes and backups.

volumes.title: Retrieval System
requirements: Support lexical, dense, hybrid, metadata, temporal, graph, code-symbol and multi-hop retrieval behind common evidence contracts.
Apply authorization/data-scope filters at query time before ranking.
Return source/version/time/provenance and make stale/partial results explicit.

volumes.title: Knowledge System
requirements: Represent entity, relation, claim, evidence, scope, time and source separately.
Allow contradictory claims to coexist with explicit provenance rather than destructive overwrite.
Support reconciliation and snapshots without erasing historical truth state.
gaps: define confidence/verification interaction without collapsing them

volumes.title: Cognitive Core
requirements: Select bounded cognitive strategies based on task, risk, budget and available evidence.
Record structured decision state sufficient for replay/eval without depending on hidden reasoning text.
Enforce stopping rules across search, reflection, critique and repair.

volumes.title: Planning Engine
requirements: Represent plans as dependency DAGs with preconditions, postconditions, capabilities, budgets and deadlines.
Statically detect cycles, unreachable nodes, missing capabilities and absent terminal behavior.
Support simulation/critical-path analysis without bypassing authority constraints.

volumes.title: Tool & Action System
requirements: Treat every tool as a privileged execution surface with independent authorization.
Validate input/output schemas, classification, risk, budget and idempotency before execution.
Bind postconditions and durable receipts to the originating operation.
gaps: normalize all connectors onto one invocation contract

volumes.title: Agent Runtime
requirements: Define agent identity, role, objective scope, authority, capability set, memory policy and resource limits.
Require delegated authority to be a mechanical subset of parent authority.
Persist lifecycle/checkpoint state for cancellation, recovery and audit.

volumes.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
requirements: Coordinate multiple agents with explicit handoff packets, leases/fencing, conflict domains and bounded fan-out.
Resolve disagreement by evidence/verification policy rather than majority text alone.
Prevent mutation collisions and stale workers from committing.

volumes.title: Long-Horizon Autonomy
requirements: Support long-running operations with durable checkpoints, resumable plans, deadline/budget enforcement and human override.
Make pause/wait/retry states explicit and recoverable after process/node restarts.
Detect goal drift and require re-authorization when objective/authority context materially changes.
gaps: human override UX/API must be unified

volumes.title: World Models & Simulation
requirements: Keep simulation/world-model state clearly separated from real-world authority and side effects.
Represent uncertainty and model assumptions in simulated transitions.
Use simulation for planning/challenge without allowing simulated success to count as real postcondition evidence.

volumes.title: Multimodal Intelligence
requirements: Use typed modality contracts for images, documents, audio, speech and video with provenance and classification.
Preserve cross-modal alignment and source identity when extracting or transforming content.
Treat hidden/embedded instructions and metadata as untrusted evidence, not policy.

volumes.title: Code Intelligence
requirements: Build repository intelligence from files, symbols, imports, ownership, tests and change history.
Track index freshness and provenance so stale code graphs are visible.
Provide impact queries without treating heuristic dependency inference as certainty.
gaps: connect ownership/test mapping to change planner

volumes.title: Autonomous Repository Engineering
requirements: Use inspect→plan→lease→edit→build→test→review→verify as the canonical repository mutation flow.
Isolate workspaces and mutation leases to prevent concurrent destructive edits.
Require patch provenance, focused regression evidence and rollback/revert path.
gaps: independent reviewer/verifier routing needs full integration

volumes.title: Forge
requirements: Generate code/policy/prompt/config/artifact candidates only inside bounded experiment scopes.
Compare candidates against champion baselines using explicit acceptance metrics.
Prevent forge candidates from directly mutating production.
gaps: standard candidate artifact schema needs integration

volumes.title: Learning & Evolution
requirements: Collect learning signals with source, scope, confidence and outcome provenance.
Turn signals into versioned candidates rather than direct production mutation.
Measure regressions, distribution shift and rollback safety before promotion.
gaps: online adaptation remains experimental until rollback evidence exists

volumes.title: Safety Architecture
requirements: Maintain explicit hazard/risk taxonomy and safe default behavior for high-impact operations.
Separate safety policy from model preference/confidence.
Provide human override/escalation paths without allowing silent authority escalation.
gaps: system-level hazard analysis needs formal artifact

volumes.title: Cybersecurity
requirements: Enforce least privilege, secret isolation, sandboxing, egress control and supply-chain integrity across model/tool/CI/runtime boundaries.
Authorize normalized resources at the last responsible moment to resist TOCTOU and parsing differentials.
Keep secrets referenced rather than copied into prompts/logs/artifacts.
gaps: bind runtime tool permissions to capability-security primitives

volumes.title: Privacy & Data Protection
requirements: Classify data at ingestion and preserve classification through derived artifacts.
Implement retention, deletion, export and residency semantics across source, projection, embedding, cache and backup.
Minimize data exposure to providers/tools by policy.
gaps: prove deletion through all future derived stores

volumes.title: Governance & Authority
requirements: Represent identities, roles, grants, approvals and delegation as explicit versioned authority objects.
Require child/delegated authority to be a subset with expiry and revocation semantics.
Audit every privileged decision with policy version and evidence.

volumes.title: Reliability
requirements: Use bounded retry/backoff/jitter, circuit breakers, bulkheads, queues, DLQ and load shedding as explicit policies.
Treat timeout as unknown outcome unless a postcondition proves failure/success.
Preserve availability without violating correctness or authority.
gaps: connect SLO/error-budget state to admission control

volumes.title: Distributed Systems
requirements: Model partitions, ordering, leases/fencing, clocks, idempotency and consistency choices explicitly.
Ensure stale workers cannot commit after lease loss.
Define remote execution/message semantics under duplication, delay, reordering and partial failure.

volumes.title: Compute & Hardware
requirements: Inventory CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM/storage/network/NUMA/interconnect resources with freshness.
Admit/place work using hard resource constraints before optimization preferences.
Handle OOM, device reset, thermal throttling and heterogeneous hardware explicitly.
gaps: resource reservation must bind to scheduler

volumes.title: High-Performance Native Core
requirements: Use native acceleration only behind stable capability/ABI boundaries with safe fallback.
Require memory/thread safety and deterministic error translation across FFI.
Version ABI and platform feature detection.
gaps: select acceleration targets by profiling evidence
expand isolation strategy for crash-prone native code

volumes.title: Java / JVM Plane
requirements: Use JVM components only where they provide measured interoperability/performance/operational benefit.
Define serialization, lifecycle, backpressure and failure boundaries between Python/native/JVM planes.
Prevent classpath/config/runtime drift from changing core semantics.
gaps: identify workloads where JVM is actually beneficial

volumes.title: Observability
requirements: Correlate logs, metrics, traces, model/tool usage and durable receipts by operation identity.
Redact secrets/sensitive data before emission.
Make one operation reconstructable without relying on ephemeral process memory.
gaps: unify event/trace IDs across all surfaces

volumes.title: Evaluation Program
requirements: Version every benchmark/eval with dataset, config, environment, model, inference budget and statistical method.
Track contamination and baseline provenance.
Separate capability, regression, system, long-horizon and production-outcome evals.
gaps: define canonical statistical policy by metric type

volumes.title: Adversarial Evaluation
requirements: Maintain adversarial cases mapped to threat/edge obligations and capability owners.
Keep adversarial judge/verifier independence measurable.
Promote discovered failures into durable regression cases.
risks: false sense of safety from static corpus
gaps: link every P0/P1 risk to executable adversarial evidence where applicable

volumes.title: Verification Plane
requirements: Represent verification separately from generator confidence and acceptance policy.
Support structural, evidence, postcondition, execution, mathematical, independent-model and human verification modes.
Bind verdicts to claim/action/artifact versions and evidence.

volumes.title: Provenance
requirements: Track end-to-end lineage from source/user input through context/model/tool/agent/artifact/output.
Canonicalize before hashing/signing and version the canonicalization algorithm.
Preserve lineage through transforms, copies, caches and release artifacts.

volumes.title: Event Architecture
requirements: Use versioned event envelopes with stable identity, causation/correlation and ordering metadata.
Implement transactional outbox/inbox where events bridge durable state and async consumers.
Support replay, compaction and schema evolution without duplicating side effects.
risks: consumer side effect before inbox marker

volumes.title: Streaming
requirements: Define resumable streaming with stable event IDs, sequence semantics, cursors and terminal finality.
Bound server/client buffering with backpressure and resync behavior.
Reconcile provisional UI content against authoritative terminal state.
gaps: bind frontend reducer evidence into canonical release suite

edge_historical.policy: Map cases into existing volumes and promote relevant entries to executable tests/invariants/evidence during implementation.

p0_edge_case_matrix.policy: Mapped edge/historical obligations must become executable evidence or explicit accepted risk before hardening.

full_edge_case_matrix.coverage: all 240 catalogue entries have one or more W00-W30 owners
full_edge_case_matrix.policy: Critical/high cases require executable evidence or explicit accepted-risk disposition before hardened/production state.

accountability.rule: No tracked plan item may be represented as complete without validated checkbox, UTC timestamped implementation signoff, independent verification signoff, git revision and evidence.

build_depth_sequence.rule: Construction waves order and gate work; they do not replace AIQ dependencies, gap closure, vertical-slice evidence, or signed accountability.

specified.meaning: scope and canonical identity are defined; implementation may not exist

scaffolded.meaning: requirements and intended capability/contract shape are explicit enough to build

implemented.meaning: code/config exists behind declared contracts with focused tests

integrated.meaning: implementation participates in assembled runtime with integration evidence

hardened.meaning: failure, security, recovery and mapped high-impact edge obligations are closed or explicitly accepted

production.meaning: release/rollback/operations/SLO evidence exists and signed accountability is complete

experimental.meaning: bounded research candidate; must not be treated as production authority

retired.meaning: removed from active production authority with retained lineage/evidence

volume_maturity_policy.promotion_rule: Status promotion is invalid unless all fields required by the target maturity state are non-empty and signed accountability permits the corresponding implementation_status.
volume_maturity_policy.anti_shortcut: File existence, LOC, a passing happy path, or documentation alone cannot satisfy a maturity promotion.

depth_passes.title: Foundational architecture-to-streaming depth pass
depth_passes.evidence_policy: evidence may remain empty while implementation_status is unverified; evidence must become non-empty under the volume maturity promotion policy before verified+ states.
depth_passes.purpose: Replace title-only placeholders in the foundational 41 volumes with buildable requirements, contracts, test/eval intent, risks and known gaps.
